validity.recommendation: No existence/classification/duplicate problem. This is the country note's own 'reference case' phase pair (P0938 operating 365 km + P3602 construction 1,517 km) and it matches the PNGRB register on both halves. See the separate spec/attribution flags below and the status_reviews entry for the real caveat (probable staleness).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed via multiple independent origins, not a phantom. (1) Oil & Gas Journal, 6 Aug 2012, 'GSPL India lets engineering contract for 2,000-km natural gas pipeline' -- trade press covering GITL's award of an engineering contract for this exact corridor (verified live, url_verifier OK). (2) Offshore Technology market-data page 'Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur Phase II, India' -- an independent commercial database entry naming this project as 'Phase II' specifically, matching GEM's own segment label (verified live, url_verifier OK). (3) PNGRB's own regulator documents (Annual Report 2019-20 p.109-111 Sr.No.6 of the partly-commissioned table; the live 31-May-2026 NGPL MIS register Sr.No.3 of the partially-commissioned section; a PNGRB Board letter dated 21.06.2019 Ref Infra/PL/Monitoring/MBBVPL/05; and GITL's own PNGRB Schedule-1 capacity-declaration filing dated 01.01.2021) all independently corroborate the same authorization: entity GSPL India Transco Limited (GITL), authorised 07.07.2011, corridor Mallavaram (AP) via Bhopal/Ramagundam through to Bhilwara-Vijaipur. CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission, common-carrier -- matches PNGRB's own regulatory classification throughout. DUPLICATE: checked against all 26 other roster rows. P0938 (Phase I, same pipeline name, 365 km operating) is NOT a duplicate of P3602 -- it is a legitimate phased split of one authorisation, exactly the shape the country's PNGRB register itself uses ('Natural Gas Pipelines Partly Commissioned'): the register's Sr.No.3/6 entry gives operating 364-365 km and under-construction 1,517 km against the SAME single authorisation number, which is precisely P0938+P3602. No other roster row (P0905 Anjar-Chotila, P1434 Kakinada-Vijayawada-Nellore, etc.) overlaps this corridor. Confirms the country note's characterisation of this pair as the 'reference case' for legitimate phase splits.

validity.recommendation: Verify EndLocation/EndState-Province. Bhopal is the capital of Madhya Pradesh, not Rajasthan, so 'EndPrefecture/District: Bhopal' + 'EndState/Province: Rajasthan' on the same row is an internal contradiction. The pipeline's own name places its actual terminus at Vijaipur (a town in Guna district, Madhya Pradesh -- site of GAIL's Vijaipur petrochemical complex), which is currently not recorded in EndLocation at all.
validity.researcher_notes: The unit's Location [ref] cluster is irregular=true and MISSING_REF, and on inspection the values look internally inconsistent rather than just unsourced: StartLocation=Mallavaram/AP (correct), but EndPrefecture/District=Bhopal paired with EndState/Province=Rajasthan -- Bhopal is the state capital of Madhya Pradesh, a well-known fact independent of any single source, so it cannot simultaneously sit in 'Rajasthan'. PNGRB's own Annual Report 2019-20 table (Sr.No.6) lists the states the corridor passes through as 'Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan' -- i.e. Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are BOTH on the route as distinct states, consistent with Bhopal (MP) being a waypoint and Bhilwara/Vijaipur (Rajasthan/Madhya Pradesh respectively) being further down the line, not with Bhopal itself being 'in Rajasthan'. Given the pipeline's own name orders the four points Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur, the actual final terminus is Vijaipur, which general geography places in Guna district, Madhya Pradesh, not Rajasthan -- but I could not independently re-confirm Vijaipur's district/state with a fresh citable source this session (web search budget exhausted), so I am flagging for human verification rather than proposing a specific replacement value.

validity.recommendation: Verify Owner1/Owner1% on both P3602 and its sibling P0938. Every PNGRB document names the authorised entity as 'GSPL India Transco Limited (GITL)', not 'Gujarat State Petronet' directly -- and GITL-type PNGRB SPVs from this 2011 authorisation round were typically multi-party consortiums (GSPL plus other PSU gas majors), not 100%-parent-owned, though I could not pin down the exact current shareholding split this session.
validity.researcher_notes: Three independent PNGRB documents all name the authorised/operating entity as 'GSPL India Transco Limited' (GITL): the 21.06.2019 PNGRB extension letter (addressed to 'Shri N. Bose Babu, Chief Executive Officer, GSPL India Transco Limited'), GITL's own PNGRB Schedule-1 capacity declaration filed 01.01.2021 ('Name of entity: GSPL India Transco Limited'), and the PNGRB Annual Report 2019-20 authorisation table (Sr.No.6, 'GSPL India Transco Limited'). The sheet instead records Owner1='Gujarat State Petronet' at 100%. GSPL (the parent, Gujarat State Petronet Limited) and GITL (the project SPV) are related but distinct legal entities, and the 2011-vintage PNGRB pipeline SPVs of this type (GITL for this corridor, GIGL for Mehsana-Bhatinda/Bhatinda-Jammu-Srinagar) were set up as multi-party consortiums among GSPL and other state/PSU gas companies rather than as GSPL's own 100%-owned subsidiaries -- so both the entity name (GITL vs GSPL) and the 100% figure look potentially wrong, though I did not find a document this session that states GITL's actual current shareholding percentages, so I am not proposing a replacement value. Note this same Owner1='Gujarat State Petronet'/100% pattern is also on sibling row P0938 (Phase I) -- if this is a real defect it likely affects both rows.

fills.researcher_notes: Lead only, not staged as a value: PNGRB's 21.06.2019 extension letter (Ref Infra/PL/Monitoring/MBBVPL/05) instructs the shipper/transporter to 'simulate the flow considering 42" diameter pipeline as per the original conditions of authorization', i.e. the corridor's ORIGINAL authorised design spec was 42-inch. But the same letter records that the portion actually built (the 363-365 km Phase I / P0938 stretch) was laid at a deviated 18-inch instead, and paragraph 6 contemplates a future 'loop line' rather than necessarily completing the original 42-inch balance corridor -- i.e. it is not clear the still-unbuilt 1,517 km balance (P3602) will ever be built to the original 42-inch spec, if it is built at all (see the status_reviews dormancy finding). Given that live uncertainty, staging Diameter=42 on P3602 specifically would risk asserting a design spec for pipe that may never get laid as originally planned, so I am leaving this blank and flagging the lead for a human rather than fabricating a value on a weak/contested field.

summary: P3602 (Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur Phase II) is a real, well-corroborated authorization and NOT a duplicate of its legitimate phase-pair sibling P0938 -- but Status='construction' looks stale: PNGRB's own 2019 extension letter, 2019-20 Annual Report and live May-2026 register all show the same lapsed March-2020 target and zero weld/hydrotest/lower progress on the 1,517 km balance for 6+ years, the identical pattern the country already treats as grounds for 'shelved' on P0921 -- proposing shelved (inferred), flagging a possible stronger cancellation finding for follow-up, plus attribution concerns on EndState/Province (Bhopal is Madhya Pradesh, not Rajasthan) and Owner1 (documents name 'GSPL India Transco Limited', not 'Gujarat State Petronet', as the authorised entity).
